To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we can: (1) fuse documents that belong to the same individual or organization, (2) detect attempts at deliberate obfuscated data, and (3) fuse new documents incrementally.

(1) we can improve accuracy of fusion of documents by using inter document references; (2) the fusion of documents can be performed incrementally; and (3) the fusion of the documents is robust to deliberate obfuscation of the documents.

(1) inter document references can improve the accuracy of fusion by up to 20% over using only attribute similarity, and (2) inter document references are also very effective in detecting attempts at obfuscation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How do we fuse entities across documents that are likely to belong to a single individual? What is the best way to incrementally update the fused entity collection? How can we use inter document references to improve the fusion process?
the problem of fusing multiple documents into a single entity document, where each document is represented as a set of attributes and the documents are linked to each other by references.
the problem of fusing information from linked documents to create a consolidated profile of entities, and in particular to detect and resolve deliberate obfuscation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the algorithm described in the paper is an efficient and effective way to perform incremental fusion of entity documents, and the performance and accuracy is improved by using inter document references.
our technique is able to fuse documents from multiple sources, with and without inter document references, to produce a unique profile for an individual with a high degree of accuracy.
our approach to entity fusion is a significant improvement over the prior art, especially for incremental document collections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a system for fusing documents from multiple sources that can be used in a real world setting, and we have developed a set of metrics to evaluate its performance.
we have demonstrated that inter document references can be effectively used to identify entities and that the use of such information can improve the accuracy of the fusion process.
we have developed an efficient and scalable technique to fuse entities in a corpus of documents that can be incrementally updated with new documents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inter document references can help improve the accuracy of entity fusion, especially when the data sources are not very reliable, and also to detect attempts to hide the identity of entities.
by exploiting references between documents, one can improve the accuracy and robustness of the fusion process.
we can achieve high precision and recall by exploiting references to other documents that are known to refer to the same entity.
